a16z's Moses Sternstein on why "there is no Gen Z":

"If you take Gen Z and you put them in a room of 99 other Gen Zs, 99 other millennials, 99 other Gen X, 99 other boomers, the odds of them finding a perfect match are almost the same. They actually have a slightly higher likelihood of matching with Gen X and boomers than they do with Gen Z."

"It's definitely heterogeneity, but it also just might be there are more Gen Z tribes... If you're trying to find some kind of uniform cohort, you're just not gonna find it."

"They are fragmented by their different online, by their internet consumption."

"And the implication, whether for politics, for marketing, for institutional trust is, everybody keeps asking, how do we reach the youngs? How do we reach these kids? But the issue is that of course, there is no Gen Z, so it's a hard problem to solve."

@MosesSternstein @alex_danco

tweets.text:
US stocks have rarely been this oversold:

The S&P 500 closed the week 4.1 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average, its widest deviation since August 2015.

This also marks its 3rd-largest deviation in at least 20 years.

By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis, the index’s largest deviation from its 50-DMA was 3.6 standard deviations.

Not even the 2020 Pandemic crash saw such extreme oversold conditions, with the S&P 500 falling 3.8 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average in February.

During the 2022 bear market and the April 2025 post-"Liberation Day" selloff, the S&P 500 fell 3.2 and 3.3 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average, respectively.

This has been one of the sharpest market sell-offs in history.
